blocks.x: Data & Lakehouse applied to Capabilities. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

In Retail & Consumer Goods, data, analytics & lakehouse is the substrate tower: pipeline modernization, lakehouse architecture on databricks and snowflake, streaming and event-driven decisioning, executive bi, master data and cataloging, predictive analytics, and data products that generate revenue. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: data engineering & pipeline modernization, lakehouse architecture & migration, real-time streaming & event-driven decisioning — delivered on Dataq Forge and Dataq Nexus with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: Demand signals too slow
Batch demand models react to last week; promotions, weather and local events shift baskets daily. Markdown decisions and replenishment both inherit the lag.
Retail media measurement contested
Vendors claim incrementality with last-touch logic; the retailer cannot arbitrate because clean-room measurement does not exist.
Personalization without privacy architecture
Personalization programs stall between marketing ambition and privacy office veto; consent, preference and profiling rules are retrofitted after launch.

blocks.x: How we deliver it in this sector

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: GDPR/CCPA and consent regimes and Price-transparency/consumer-protection rules. Dynamic pricing constraints by jurisdiction. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

The engagement cadence below is the standard pattern for this capability. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
